evidence: Liv. 22.39.19: vēritātem labōrāre nimis saepe ajunt, exstinguī numquam
Cic. Off. 1.109: vēritātis cultōrēs, fraudis inimīcī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Truth as a thing in itself, and truthfulness as a quality: Lewis & Short note that it is “always abstract”. It also means reality as against imitation (see reality). The truth one tells, asks for or finds out is usually vērum or vēra.

terms.gloss: the truth: what is true, the truth told
terms.grammar: noun, second declension; the neuter of vērus used as a noun
evidence: Plaut. Am. 1.1.89; Ter. An. 2.6.6: vērum dīcere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To tell the truth is vērum dīcere, or in the plural vēra dīcere (Plautus, Lewis & Short); its opposite is falsum. For the aside “to tell the truth”, ut vērum dīcam, see true.

phrases.latin: vēritātem labōrāre nimis saepe ajunt, exstinguī numquam
phrases.english: the truth, they say, is too often in trouble, but never snuffed out
going along with people makes friends; the truth makes enemies
phrases.source: Ter. An. 68, quoted in Cic. Amic. 89

phrases.latin: quīcumque turpī fraude semel innōtuit, etiam sī vērum dīcit, āmittit fidem
phrases.english: whoever has once been caught in a shameful deceit is not believed even when he tells the truth
the language of truth is simple

phrases.latin: auctōritāte advocātōrum adductī in vēritāte mānsērunt
phrases.english: persuaded by the standing of their counsel, they stuck to the truth
